scenario.title: TATSINSKAYA RAID - 22 DEC 1942
intro.text:
TATSINSKAYA RAID - 22 DEC 1942

Bol'shinka, 200km west of Stalingrad

You'll lead a raid deep into the German rear - the target is the enemy airfield at Tatsinskaya, the primary operating base for the German airlift efforts to Stalingrad. Inflict significant losses on enemy Air Force by destroying as many planes as possible and force the Germans to divert forces attempting to relieve their forces encircled in Stalingrad!

ORDERS
Reach the Exit Point with at least 8 of your ground units.

NOTES
a. You don't have to control all VH! You just have to ensure that you keep at least one VH occupied so that the enemy can't win.
b. Attention - winter conditions! If possible, equip your troops with tracked movement. Check if you can switch between wheeled and tracked movement for free.

CORE (recommended)
4x Tank
5x Infantry
2x Anti-Tank
3x Reconnaissance (+1)
2x Flak
4x Artillery
3x Fighter Aircraft
2x Tactical Bomber
header.act: ACT III — FROM DEFEAT TO OPERATIONAL MASTERY
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.reaction-briliant.text: Voronezh remained contested for every required hour, and the German spearheads spent their strength against a defence that refused to become a rout.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.reaction-victory.text: The line at Voronezh bent until the reserves arrived. The ground lost is marked in pencil; the time gained is what kept the front intact.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.reaction-tactical.text: We bought the ten turns at Voronezh with nearly every reserve we possessed. The men now assigned to raid Tatsinskaya are the part we did not spend.
line.reaction-lose.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.reaction-lose.text: The Voronezh line broke before the reserves were ready. Headquarters is answering a failed defence with a raid deep into the enemy rear; nobody has called that contradiction by its name.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-a.text: The mobile reserve at Voronezh taught the crews to strike a spearhead without being swallowed by it. They believe the same reflex can bring them home from an airfield far behind the front.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: The strongpoints at Voronezh bought every required hour, but none had to move after the battle began. Tatsinskaya offers no position that can be held until relief arrives.
line.scene-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-0.text: Captured road signs are stacked beside the map. None points back toward friendly lines. The airfield photographs show rows of transport aircraft; the latest report shows enemy armour turning toward the same roads we need for withdrawal.
line.scene-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.scene-1.text: A breakthrough joins an army behind it. A raid cuts that thread by design. Every kilometre toward the aircraft is also a kilometre the corps may have to fight twice.
line.decision.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.decision.text: We can devote every mobile group to destroying the airlift, or assign a rear guard and open the return route before the airfield is fully wrecked. A raid succeeds only if its effect outlives its raiders.
line.decision.choice.wreck-the-airlift.t: Drive every available group onto the airfield and destroy the transports before they can disperse.
line.decision.choice.wreck-the-airlift.h: Attach an eight-strength Il-2m3 detachment with 40 experience for the airfield strike; concentrated air support costs 120 prestige.
line.decision.choice.guard-the-return.te: Assign a mobile rear guard now and preserve a marked route back to friendly lines.
line.decision.choice.guard-the-return.hi: Attach an eight-strength T-70 reconnaissance detachment with 40 experience and fully refuel the core; road-security preparations cost 70 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-a-0.text: The airfield is the centre of gravity. Demolition groups receive priority, and the column turns only after the transport rows are burning.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-a-1.text: Write the turning hour before Antonov reaches the first transport. If the demolition teams miss it, the rear guard leaves without waiting for his pride.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-b-0.text: The rear guard moves first, not last. It will seize road junctions on the way in and hold them open on the way out.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-b-1.text: The road may save the corps and leave aircraft flying into Stalingrad. I want the surviving transport rows counted, not hidden inside the word successful.
line.post-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.post-0.text: The turning hour goes in Antonov's map case before the engines start. If he opens it only at the airfield, we have already lost the argument.
